explanations: There is none. Refill is capped at burst with Math.min, so idle drivers cannot bank unlimited tokens; elapsed time is clamped at 0 and uses performance.now(), a monotonic clock, so wall-clock adjustments cannot mint tokens; the timestamp is updated on both allow and deny paths without losing fractional tokens because the stored value is the already-refilled amount; and waitMs is computed from the actual deficit. Per-driver state is removed when the driver goes offline, so the Map does not grow with churn.

With no prior state, available starts at burst (3). Each allowed ping stores available - 1, and with zero elapsed time no refill happens, so pings 1-3 pass (3, 2, 1 available) and pings 4 and 5 see 0 and are denied. Missing state means a full bucket, not an empty one.

On denial the limiter stores the refilled amount with the new timestamp, so accumulated fractions are kept (0.1 per 100 ms). After about 1 s available reaches 1 and the ping is allowed. Denials do not reset progress, they do write state, and only one token (not a full burst) is needed.

onPing validates coordinates first and returns 400 before calling limiter.allow, so invalid pings never touch the bucket and never see 429. Nothing clamps values. This means invalid traffic is not throttled by this limiter, a tradeoff that keeps bad payloads from eating a driver's budget.
